messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR prep: customer health rollercoaster & executive triage asks

Team —

Quick heads-up as I prepare the exec QBR packet for AcmeCorp (renewal in 60d): this account has bounced between "green" and "amber" the last two months due to intermittent latency during peak inference windows and a surprise spike in token usage after they rolled a new feature. I need a concise set of items for the exec slide deck by EOD tomorrow. Can each of you take the sections below and drop a one-paragraph status + one clear ask?

- Lauren: Customer health summary + top 3 technical risks (1 paragraph each)
- Jonas: Renewal risk register entries (prioritized) + suggested escalation path
- Marissa: Commercial position / recent negotiations and any outstanding procurement blockers
- Grace: CS enablement items and a short list of unresolved customer asks

Please attach any heatmaps, logs, or PRs. I attached a template for the executive asks (qbr_exec_asks.pdf) — fill only the highlighted fields. My ask: prioritize what requires executive attention (credits, SLA exception, patch timeline).

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
redwood.inference

Attachments: qbr_exec_asks.pdf (template)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-17T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: customer health rollercoaster & executive triage asks

Hannah / team —

Status (high level): AcmeCorp health is currently AMBER. Their 99th-pct latency exceeded the SLA twice in the last three weeks (both incidents correlate with a customer A/B test that increased batch sizes). They are otherwise satisfied with output quality.

Top technical risks (1-liners):
1) Peak latency spikes during concurrent batch windows — likely config+batching policy mismatch. Ask: senior infra engineer time to review batching policy and a temporary elevated concurrency cap for two weeks.
2) Token-usage surge causing monthly overages — Ask: propose a one-time cushion credit and implement token throttling guardrails.
3) KV-cache cold starts impacting long-tail prompts — Ask: schedule short-term cache-warmup script deployment before peak windows.

Attachments: acme_health_heatmap.csv (heatmap showing latency vs. traffic, last 30d)

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Principal Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the heads up. Quick context from our side: the A/B test that spiked token usage was in a three-day window; we've rolled it back but want a plan to avoid re-introducing instability when we re-run. Can you confirm whether the elevated concurrency cap would risk impacting other customers? We also need a tighter timeline for the caching fix — our SREs are ready to coordinate.

Team —

Renewal risk register (prioritized):
1) SLA breach history (2 incidents, 30d window) — Risk: High. Mitigation: Exec-level SLA exception request + operational remediation plan. Owner: Hannah + Infra.
2) Commercial friction on overage credits — Risk: Medium. Mitigation: one-time credit proposal and tighter quota alerts. Owner: Marissa.
3) Feature stability concerns from Acme SREs — Risk: Medium. Mitigation: create a joint SRE runbook and dedicated sync cadence. Owner: Grace.
4) Contract negotiation timeline (Procurement delays) — Risk: Medium-Low. Mitigation: Sales to secure procurement checkpoint this week. Owner: Marissa.

Suggested escalation path: 1) Approve temporary concurrency cap and plan (Infra sprint 72) — exec sign-off needed for cross-customer risk. 2) Approve one-time credit (finance sign-off). 3) SRE-to-SRE runbook sign-off and commit to weekly sync for 6 weeks.

I attached a short action tracker (renewal_action_items.docx) and marked the items that need exec attention.

Jonas
Director, Renewals, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR prep: customer health rollercoaster & executive triage asks

Thanks all — concise exec asks below (for slide deck):

1) Approve a temporary concurrency cap increase for AcmeCorp for 2 weeks while Infra applies batching policy updates. (Risk: cross-customer resource contention) — Owner: CTO / Ops Exec decision required by EOD tomorrow.
2) Approve a one-time usage credit to cover April overage (~$12k). Owner: Finance lead.
3) Greenlight priority SLA remediation sprint (Infra sprint 72) and standing SRE sync for 6 weeks. Owner: Infra Dir.

If exec can sign off on the three items above we will: 1) issue a formal remediation plan, 2) issue the one-time credit, and 3) commit to weekly SRE check-ins with Acme.

I'll include a single-slide risk register and call out the owner/ask for each. Marissa — please prep the commercial note for the slide. Jonas — please convert the register into a one-slide heatmap (high/med/low) and drop in the folder linked above. Lauren / Grace — please confirm the post-fix verification checklist.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
